name: Compositional Balance: Using Visual Weight with Purpose
description: Master Compositional Balance with a free 1-page . Learn symmetry, asymmetry, golden ratio and visual weight to create stronger, harmonious photos.

step.name: Choose the relationship between visual weights
step.text: Compositional balance concerns how attention is distributed across a photograph. Size, brightness, colour, detail, position and meaning all influence the visual weight of an element. A settled arrangement may express stillness. Unequal weight may create tension or make one area deliberately dominant. Consider what the relationship contributes before deciding that it needs correcting. Restraint includes resisting the urge to add a counterweight. step.name: Compose with Vision, Not Just Technique
step.text: Composition isn’t about rule-following. It’s about story-shaping. The camera captures—but you compose meaning through balance, light, framing, and intention. Great composition begins with seeing—pausing, observing, and feeling before pressing the shutter. From that place, choose your method (symmetry, asymmetry, golden ratio, size balance) to guide the viewer's inner journey, not just their eyes. Symmetry — mirror forms for calm structure; break slightly to maintain flow. Asymmetry — offset weight with tone or scale; use diagonals for energy.
